title: The desert mothers
hookLine: Amma Syncletica and others taught that the real desert is the heart

cards: Turn the pages of the desert sayings and the title you keep meeting is abba. Abba this, abba that. Then, here and there, a different one.
Amma Sarah. Amma Theodora. Amma Syncletica.

Women who went out to pray in the wilderness too, remembered not as someone's sister or helper, but as teachers in their own right. People came to them asking for a word, just as they did with the men.
And one of them moved the desert somewhere nobody expected.

teach.b: First, the title. Amma means mother. Like abba, it's not a family tie but a spiritual one: an elder whose life had taught her something worth passing on, and whose few words people carried home.
Second, one of them by name.
Tradition says Syncletica came from a well-off family in Alexandria, gave away what she had, and lived a life of prayer and fasting near the city, not deep in the sand.
Younger women gathered to learn from her, and a later writer collected her teaching into a life. Her sayings sit right beside the abbas' in the desert collection. Third, the turn.
A desert mother might be expected to say: go to the desert. Syncletica says something sharper. Some who live out on the mountain, she warns, behave as if they were in town, and they're lost.

teach.h: A CROWD IN YOUR OWN THOUGHTS.
teach.b: And it's possible to live among a crowd and be solitary in your mind, while someone living alone can be living in a crowd of her own thoughts. The quiet isn't guaranteed by the sand.
The noise isn't guaranteed by the city.
For Syncletica, the real desert, the place of prayer without distraction, is inside. Fourth, what that means on a Tuesday: a bus, a waiting room, a kitchen at dinnertime.
The desert mothers didn't promise those places would go quiet. Syncletica's saying suggests the quiet can be found in them anyway, and that a person can carry a small wilderness through a loud day.

how: Catholic women religious, including contemplative nuns, continue a life of prayer and silence, and the Church honors Saint Syncletica among the desert mothers.

o: a grandmother who teaches children to pray
mother: a title for a woman elder of the desert
a nun who leads her convent as its abbess

games.q: the desert mothers — tap the pairs.
p: some live as if in town
you can be solitary in mind

s: only men were remembered as teachers in the desert
Amma Sarah, Amma Theodora and Amma Syncletica have sayings of their own.
Syncletica said going to the desert guarantees quiet
she warned that some who live on the mountain behave as if they were in town.
Syncletica said a person living alone can live in a crowd of thoughts
and a person in a crowd can be solitary in mind.

games.q: you tell Amma Syncletica you can't find quiet because your life is too crowded. what does her teaching point to?
o: move to the mountains and leave everyone.
find the solitude in your mind, even in a crowd.
games.why: Syncletica says the place is not the point: a person can be solitary in mind among a crowd, and crowded in mind alone.

practice: Leave the noise around you as it is, traffic, voices, a fridge humming, and notice the crowd of your own thoughts, the way Syncletica describes it.
Don't chase them out; step back from them, the way you'd step off a busy street onto a doorstep. If you pray, rest in God's presence without saying anything at all.

wordCard.voice: Amma. Mother: the title the desert gave its women teachers, like Amma Syncletica. Today's word.
